{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash -l
#FLUX: --cpus-per-task=1
#FLUX: --qos=debug
#FLUX: --nodes=1
#FLUX: --time=00:30:00
#FLUX: --job-name=job-1b
#FLUX: --output=stats/job-1b.o%j
#FLUX: --error=stats/job-1b.e%j

# The Slurm directives '--constraint=knl' and '--cpu-freq=1400000' are hardware-specific requests with no direct equivalents in standard Flux and have been omitted.
# The omission of the constraint means the job may not run on the intended KNL architecture. The omission of cpu-freq means the CPU will run at the system's default frequency, which could affect performance.


# set some openmp variables: 
# OMP_PLACES=threads maps OpenMP threads to hardware threads
# OMP_PROC_BIND=spread binds threads as evenly as possible
#
# see https://docs.nersc.gov/jobs/affinity/ for more information

export OMP_PLACES=threads
export OMP_PROC_BIND=spread

export OMP_SCHEDULE=static
# export OMP_SCHEDULE=dynamic

for t in 1
   do
   export OMP_NUM_THREADS=$t
   for r in 256
      do
      for p in 1 2 4 8 16
         do
         for b in 8
            do
            # The srun command is replaced with 'flux mini run' to launch a single task.
            flux mini run -n 1 build/ray -r $r -p $p -b $b
         done
      done
   done
done
"
}

# set some openmp variables: 
# OMP_PLACES=threads maps OpenMP threads to hardware threads
# OMP_PROC_BIND=spread binds threads as evenly as possible
#
# see https://docs.nersc.gov/jobs/affinity/ for more information

export OMP_PLACES=threads
export OMP_PROC_BIND=spread

export OMP_SCHEDULE=static
# export OMP_SCHEDULE=dynamic

for t in 1
   do
   export OMP_NUM_THREADS=$t
   for r in 256
      do
      for p in 1 2 4 8 16
         do
         for b in 8
            do
            srun -n 1 build/ray -r $r -p $p -b $b
         done
      done
   done
done
